newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says Paranapanema loses Yauliyacu purchase.
newsitem.headline: Peru says Paranapanema loses Yauliyacu purchase.

text.p: Peruvian state miner Centromin said Wednesday that Brazil's Paranapanema SA Mineracao Industria e Construcao had lost its option to purchase polymetallic unit Empresa Minera Yauliyacu because it did not provide paperwork and the necessary guarantee.
"Paranapanema has lost its option on Yauliyacu because it did not send all the documents and the guarantee to take over the mine," Centromin spokesman Enrique Olivares told Reuters.
He added that the mine's sale would now be awarded to local company Minera Casapalca S.A.

Paranapanema had been given until Monday to provide the paperwork and financial guarantee before formally taking over the unit it had provisionally bought for $12.7 million at a privatization tender last December.

At the December auction, Paranapanema beat out bids from Pan American Silver Corp of Canada, Sunshine Mining and Refining Co of the United States, Glencore International AG of Switzerland and Casapalca.

Centromin had set a minimum bid price for the unit of $8 million and a minimum investment of $15 million over five years. The Brazilian mining company had offered to invest $100 million over five years.

According to Centromin, the unit has proven and probable reserves of silver, zinc, lead and copper totalling 7.3 million tonnes. The unit's potential reserves total 14.7 million tonnes. In 1995, 746,000 tonnes of mineral were extracted from the site.
